mcp.label: For Agent-Enabled Teams
mcp.heading: GST Tooling, Callable by Your AI Agents
mcp.body: Deal teams running screening through AI agents hit the same wall: an advisor's frameworks live on a website, and a website is not an interface an agent can use. GST publishes its diligence engine, portfolio record, and regulatory map as a Model Context Protocol server, so your agents call the same tools GST does: typed inputs, structured results, access provisioned per client.

audience.card2.title: SaaS Founders & Executives

engagement.heading: Typical Engagement Model
engagement.tagline: Engagements are intentionally focused to drive outcomes.
engagement.step1.label: Align
engagement.step1.text: Introductory discussion to clarify objectives, decision context, and constraints
engagement.step1.detail: Confidential, no-commitment conversation. We assess fit, understand your timeline, and identify the highest-leverage questions to answer first. Typical duration: 30 to 60 minutes.
engagement.step2.label: Define
engagement.step2.text: Focused scope aligned to decision-critical priorities
engagement.step2.detail: We design a work plan targeting your specific risk areas, whether that's a 2-week diligence sprint or a 90-day remediation roadmap. No boilerplate. Every deliverable maps to a decision you need to make.
engagement.step3.label: Deliver
engagement.step3.text: Clear findings, prioritized recommendations, and implementation-ready path forward
engagement.step3.detail: Executive-ready outputs with quantified risk, concrete remediation steps, and priority-ranked recommendations. Every finding includes severity, business impact, and a clear next action.
engagement.step4.label: Guide
engagement.step4.text: Optional ongoing advisory or execution support
engagement.step4.detail: Fractional engagement model: weekly or monthly cadence scaled to your needs. Board prep, architecture reviews, vendor evaluations, or hands-on execution alongside your team. Disengage anytime.
faq.heading: Frequently Asked Questions
faq.q1: What's the difference between buy-side and sell-side diligence?
faq.a1:
Buy-side diligence is for investors or companies acquiring a business. Is the technology sound? What will it cost to integrate, maintain, or scale? Where are the hidden risks, and where are the untapped opportunities that could accelerate growth after close (value creation)? We give you the full picture so you can negotiate from a position of knowledge.

Sell-side diligence is for founders and executives preparing to sell their company. The objective is to maximize the valuation of the company's technology in the eyes of external investors. Buyers will scrutinize everything, and unresolved issues like technical debt, security gaps, or poor documentation can reduce your price or kill a deal entirely. We work with you before going to market to fix those issues proactively, so your technology becomes a selling point rather than a liability.
faq.a2: Value creation is the process of leveraging technology to grow the business after an acquisition or investment. This can mean scaling operations to handle more customers without proportional cost increases, unlocking new revenue streams through platform capabilities, expanding market share by shipping faster than competitors, or reducing operational overhead through automation. In a PE context, value creation is where the real returns come from, not just cutting costs, but building the technology foundation that compounds growth across the hold period.
faq.q3: What does a technology due diligence engagement include?
faq.a3: A typical engagement includes a comprehensive review of the target's architecture, infrastructure, security posture, development practices, and technical team. We deliver a detailed findings report with risk quantification, remediation cost estimates, and a prioritized integration roadmap tailored to your investment thesis.
faq.q4: How long does a typical buy-side diligence take?
faq.a4: Most buy-side technical diligence engagements are completed in three to six weeks, depending on the complexity of the target's technology stack and the availability of key personnel. We can accommodate accelerated timelines for competitive deal processes when needed.
faq.q5: Can our AI agents call GST tools directly?
faq.a5: Yes. GST runs a Model Context Protocol server that exposes the diligence agenda generator, portfolio search, regulatory map, and cost and technical-debt models as callable tools, so an agent in your stack can invoke them with typed inputs and get structured results back. Access is provisioned per client rather than self-serve: GST assigns scopes and a capability tier so a deal team gets exactly the surface it needs. See the MCP Server page for the tool catalog and tiers.
faq.q6: Do you work with companies outside the US?
faq.a6: Yes. We regularly support cross-border transactions and have conducted diligence on targets across North America, Europe, and Asia-Pacific. Our frameworks are designed to evaluate distributed teams, multi-region infrastructure, and varying regulatory environments.
